findings.reason: a coordinator copying the heading into a dispatch brief would task a node with a git-process reduction its own evidence shows is unnecessary, and the section's Why omits the whole-ledger fallback that §24's ≤10 s cold target must still absorb, so the mechanism as written is not the cost the evidence reports.
findings.text: §21 is titled "Held-worktree records are found without a git process per record" and its Why concludes "Inside `_held_worktree_records` the time is matching", but the node it cites (`r-20261016T223039066944`) established that base spawns exactly one git process (the `_registered_worktrees` registry read) and that the remaining profile spawns belong to `recovery_review_subject._reviewed_run_head`/`_resolve_commit`, siblings of `_held_worktree_records` inside `_fleet`, i.e. §23's cost; that node's own accounting puts the section's cost in `ledger.runs`' whole-ledger fallback, 2,693 per-run-file reads and `_names_worktree` over 58,620 pairs — and §21 names only the matching, never the fallback that the cited evidence lists as a co-equal or dominant cost

findings.reason: the measure as written does not pin the property the deliverable asserts, so the negative control (a base-tree copy failing the count) can be satisfied by a change that leaves the matching loop intact.
findings.text: §21's done-when measures only "the path resolutions made for retained paths during one `_held_worktree_records` call", bounded at one per record, but `record_names_worktree` (routing.py:1035-1038) resolves a path only for a record carrying a `worktree_retention`; a record naming a tree by node id alone resolves nothing, so a node that memoises each retained-path resolution and keeps the O(records×trees) `_holding_record` loop over `(*rows, *records)` can pass the count bound while costing the product the deliverable ("proportional to records plus trees, not their product") exists to remove

findings.reason: without a miss-clause the node can report an unmet freshness bound with no next step, leaving the plan's stated goal ("to stay inside the 120 s freshness window") unmet and unforwarded, whereas the same miss under §6's clause would file the repair.
findings.text: §24 states two head bounds (first call ≤10 s node-local, second call <30 s GPFS) and a control that fires only when base *meets* the second bound, but gives no consequence for the case where the head arm *misses* a bound — which §20 may show is likely if the lag is filesystem-dominated, since §21–§23 cut compute, not file reads; §6's own done-when supplies the missing pattern ("a missed target ... the repair is proposed as a new section") and §24 omits it
